text: When you build a REST API, clear design matters. Start by giving your endpoints simple, meaningful names, such as /users or /orders. Use the right HTTP methods and return proper status codes, like 200 for success or 404 when something is not found. Good documentation helps other developers understand how to use your API quickly. It is also wise to add versioning, for example /v1/users, so future changes do not break existing apps. Finally, keep your responses consistent and easy to read. Following these best practices makes your API reliable and pleasant for others to work with.
